visual_elements.description: Two-dimensional one-vs-all classification plot. Three straight decision boundaries cross the plot: a red line labeled d₁(x) descending from upper-left to lower-right; a green line labeled d₂(x) ascending from lower-left to upper-right; a blue line labeled d₃(x) ascending more steeply from lower-left to upper-right. Three shaded half-plane regions are shown: C₁ (light green #90EE90 diagonal hatching, top region) containing green circular dots; C₂ (light blue #ADD8E6 diagonal hatching, right region) containing blue circular dots; C₃ (light red/pink #FFB6C1 diagonal hatching, bottom-left region) containing red circular dots. Each boundary has a '+ ve' text annotation with a colored arrow indicating the positive side: red '+ ve' near the lower-right end of the red line, green '+ ve' near the left side of the green line, blue '+ ve' near the upper-right end of the blue line.
visual_elements.position: center, spanning roughly 18% to 83% of slide width and 22% to 92% of slide height

typography_notes: Sans-serif font throughout. Title is bold, two lines: line 1 'Multi-Class Classification using' in dark red #C00000; line 2 '[ONE VS ALL] Binary Classifiers' with '[ONE VS ALL]' in blue #0000FF and 'Binary Classifiers' in dark red #C00000. Class labels C₁/C₂/C₃ are bold black text inside yellow #FFFF00 rectangles. Decision-boundary labels d₁(x)/d₂(x)/d₃(x) use their line colors (red #FF0000 / green #008000 / blue #0000FF) with subscript numerals. '+ ve' annotations are colored to match their boundary lines (red/green/blue) — the original typography_notes claimed black, which was overridden per the more specific visual_elements description (see validation.uncertain_items).
animation_state: static; no mid-build or partial-reveal indicators visible.
recreation_brief:
1. Set the slide background to solid light gray #E6E6E6. Note: this slide has NO bullet text, footer, or body paragraphs — only the elements placed in steps 2–23.
2. Place a title text box at top center (spanning most of the slide width, top ~2–15% of slide height). Type line 1 exactly: 'Multi-Class Classification using' — bold sans-serif, dark red #C00000.
3. In the same title text box, type line 2 exactly: '[ONE VS ALL] Binary Classifiers' — bold sans-serif, with '[ONE VS ALL]' in blue #0000FF and 'Binary Classifiers' in dark red #C00000.
4. In the top-right corner, draw a circle with a thin black outline and white fill containing the black text '7' (slide number).
5. Draw the plot frame: a white #FFFFFF rectangle with a thin red #FF0000 border, spanning approx. 18%–83% of slide width and 22%–92% of slide height (the large central plot area).
6. Inside the frame, draw the red decision boundary: a straight red #FF0000 line descending from the upper-left area to the lower-right area of the plot. No arrowheads on the line.
7. Draw the green decision boundary: a straight green #008000 line ascending from the lower-left area to the upper-right area of the plot. No arrowheads on the line.
8. Draw the blue decision boundary: a straight blue #0000FF line ascending from the lower-left area to the upper-right area at a visibly steeper angle than the green line. No arrowheads on the line.
9. Label the red line: place the text 'd₁(x)' in red #FF0000 (sans-serif, subscript numeral) near the upper-left end of the red line.
10. Label the green line: place the text 'd₂(x)' in green #008000 (sans-serif, subscript numeral) near the right side of the green line.
11. Label the blue line: place the text 'd₃(x)' in blue #0000FF (sans-serif, subscript numeral) near the upper-right end of the blue line.
12. Shade the top region of the plot with light green #90EE90 diagonal hatching — this is region C₁.
13. Shade the right region of the plot with light blue #ADD8E6 diagonal hatching — this is region C₂.
14. Shade the bottom-left region of the plot with light pink #FFB6C1 diagonal hatching — this is region C₃.
15. Place a small yellow #FFFF00 rectangle containing bold black text 'C₁' inside the top green-hatched region.
16. Place a small yellow #FFFF00 rectangle containing bold black text 'C₂' inside the right blue-hatched region.
17. Place a small yellow #FFFF00 rectangle containing bold black text 'C₃' inside the bottom-left pink-hatched region.
18. Scatter green #008000 filled circular dots inside the C₁ region (source does not specify the exact count; use ~8 dots as a placeholder and adjust to match the original frame's density).
19. Scatter blue #0000FF filled circular dots inside the C₂ region (same placeholder rule, ~8 dots).
20. Scatter red #FF0000 filled circular dots inside the C₃ region (same placeholder rule, ~8 dots).
21. Add the red positive-side annotation: the text '+ ve' in red #FF0000 with a short red arrow, placed near the lower-right end of the red line, arrow pointing to the positive side of the boundary.
22. Add the green positive-side annotation: the text '+ ve' in green #008000 with a short green arrow, placed near the left side of the green line, arrow pointing to the positive side of the boundary.
23. Add the blue positive-side annotation: the text '+ ve' in blue #0000FF with a short blue arrow, placed near the upper-right end of the blue line, arrow pointing to the positive side of the boundary.
24. FINAL CHECK: confirm the only text on the slide is the two title lines, '7', 'd₁(x)', 'd₂(x)', 'd₃(x)', 'C₁', 'C₂', 'C₃', and the three '+ ve' annotations; add nothing else.

fixes_applied: Rewrote recreation_brief as a 24-step ordered checklist with one element per step, exact hex colors, positions, and verbatim strings.

Resolved internal contradiction on '+ ve' color: typography_notes said black while visual_elements specifies red/green/blue per boundary; adopted the colored per-line values from visual_elements in typography_notes and the brief.
Removed 'arrowheads at the ends of each line' from the brief — visual_elements describes plain straight boundaries; arrows exist only in the '+ ve' annotations.
Added the plot-frame coordinates (18%–83% of width, 22%–92% of height) from visual_elements.position into layout.arrangement and the brief.
Replaced all color words with exact hex codes throughout (title #C00000, lines #FF0000/#008000/#0000FF, hatching #90EE90/#ADD8E6/#FFB6C1, label boxes #FFFF00, frame #FFFFFF).
Extended colors.accents to include the hatch fills (#90EE90, #ADD8E6, #FFB6C1) and plot background (#FFFFFF) so every diagram color is captured in the colors object.
Replaced the vague dot description with explicit per-region dot placement and a flagged placeholder count (~8 per region), since the source gives no exact counts.
Confirmed verbatim_text.bullets is legitimately empty (diagram-only slide with no bullet text in source, not an extraction gap); all verbatim strings are captured in labels/equations.
Added an explicit 'no other text' final-check step to prevent invented bullets, footers, or extra labels during recreation.
